title: Say plainly when nothing was logged

problem.text: Benchmark spec, written from the codebase (no member wrote it).

change.summary: In agent/src/life.js, weekText(p, now) ends with the line "Logged in the last 7 days: 0 sessions" when the player logged nothing in the past 7 days. Make that line say "Nothing logged in the last 7 days." when there are no sessions. With one or more sessions the line stays exactly as it is ("Logged in the last 7 days: 2 sessions, 90 min"), and the rest of the text does not change.

oracle.how: weekText(p) with no logs ends with "Nothing logged in the last 7 days."; with one or two sessions the whole text is the same as before.

title: Drop a court reason that is too long

problem.text: Benchmark spec, written from the codebase (no member wrote it).

change.summary: In agent/src/places.js, judge() asks Muse Glimmer for reasons of "one short sentence" each, but the code that keeps the model's reasons cuts any reason to 200 characters (String(r.text).slice(0, 200)), so a long reason reaches the player cut off. Make that code drop a reason whose text is longer than 160 characters, the way it drops a reason that fails its other checks. Nothing else changes.

oracle.how: With a judge model that answers one reason of 100 characters and one of 170, judge() keeps only the first; when every reason is too long, the rules judge the place.

privacy: No player data: a length check on the model's reasons.

title: Flooded courts count as unplayable

problem.text: Benchmark spec, written from the codebase (no member wrote it).

change.summary: In agent/src/places.js, rules(p, sport, start, w) lowers a place's score when its reviews mention something broken, missing or closed ("Reviews mention something broken, missing or closed."). A review that mentions a flooded court or puddles should count the same way: add "flooded" and "puddles" (and "puddle") to that check. The other checks stay as they are.

oracle.how: rules() for a place whose review says the court is flooded, or has puddles, gives the reason "Reviews mention something broken, missing or closed." and a lower verdict than with no review; a review that says the court is great does not.

privacy: No player data: a rule on reviews.

title: Indoor courts only, when asked

problem.text: Benchmark spec, written from the codebase (no member wrote it).

change.summary: Add an optional indoorOnly parameter to the Autopilot's find_places tool. In agent/src/places.js, search() takes an optional indoorOnly (default false): when it is true, only places that are not outdoor (by the outdoor() rule in that file) are judged and returned. In agent/src/autopilot.js, the find_places entry in TOOLS declares an optional boolean parameter indoorOnly (not required), and tools.find_places passes it on to places.search. Without indoorOnly everything works as before.

oracle.how: places.search({ ..., indoorOnly: true }) on a cached map with indoor and outdoor places judges and returns only places with outdoor false: the court judge's model is never asked about an outdoor place. Without indoorOnly every place is judged and returned. autopilot.js declares indoorOnly as an optional boolean for find_places and passes it to places.search.

privacy: No player data: a filter on public places.

title: At most so many calendar entries a day

problem.text: Benchmark spec, written from the codebase (no member wrote it).

change.summary: In agent/src/life.js, upcoming(p, days, now) returns the player's calendar entries from the start of today until days days from now. Add a maxPerDay guard: an optional fourth parameter maxPerDay (a whole number). When it is given, at most that many entries are returned for any one date (the first ones of that date, in the list's order). When it is not given, upcoming returns exactly what it returns today.

oracle.how: upcoming(p, 7, now, 1) gives one entry per date, upcoming(p, 7, now, 2) at most two, in order; upcoming(p, 7, now) gives every entry in the window, as before.

privacy: The player's own calendar, read by the player's own agent only.

title: When you last played at each usual time

problem.text: Benchmark spec, written from the codebase (no member wrote it).

change.summary: In agent/src/autopilot.js, habits(history) returns each habitual time with day, start, count, weeks, share, minutes and sport. Add one field to each: last, the date (YYYY-MM-DD) of the latest game in the history at that day and start time (the history is not always in date order). Then the get_week tool's result carries it: each entry of habitualTimes gets lastPlayed, the habit's last. The other fields stay as they are.

oracle.how: habits(history) on an unsorted history gives each entry last, the latest date at that day and start, with count, share, minutes and sport unchanged; get_week's habitualTimes entries include lastPlayed.

privacy: The player's own game dates, shown to the player's own agent only.
